sections.html:
Butler County's seat, Hamilton, lies 20 miles from Cincinnati on the Great Miami River. Prices run low, renters occupy many homes, and plenty of owners are dealing with an inherited house, a tired rental or an aging property that needs work.

Any sale involves four things: the city's building and planning staff, the short-term rental code if travelers ever stayed in the house, the state disclosure law, and the deed desk at the Butler County Auditor. Each has its own section.

The typical Hamilton home is valued at $165,200, and owners live in just 54.3% of homes. Small landlords and first-time buyers shop in this range. Many buyers are weighing your house against the cost of simply continuing to rent.

Dayton Lane, German Village and Rossville are the city's three historic districts and hold much of the oldest housing. Anyone changing the outside of a house in one of these districts, or of a listed property, first needs a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Architectural Design Review Board. Say so up front if you are in a district, since a buyer's exterior plans will go through that board.

Hamilton City Schools serve most of the city, and Hamilton High School is the main public high school. A few pockets belong to the Talawanda and Ross Local districts, so verify your street's district before an ad names a school.

Floods have hit the valley for centuries, and the worst came in March 1913. If your parcel is close to the river, find out its flood zone designation from city or county staff.

Hamilton's Building Department takes permit applications at building@hamilton-oh.gov and answers questions at (513) 785-7360. The Planning Department, at 513-785-7350, handles zoning, conditional use and variance questions. Electric, plumbing, HVAC, gas and sewer jobs call for a registered contractor. If a past owner did that kind of work, ask the Building Department whether the permit was finished, so a buyer's inspector does not find an open file you did not know about.

The permits page describes a yearly vacant building registration, with a fee that grows each year, aimed at commercial and industrial buildings. A sitting-empty house might be caught by it, so ask first.

Settling an estate often takes a certified death certificate, and the city's Vital Statistics office issues certified birth and death certificates at $25 per copy.

Chapter 758 of the city code governs stays under 30 days. A host needs a license before operating or advertising. If travelers ever stayed in the house, get the license situation straight before listing, because a buyer's agent may raise it.

  • Owner-occupied accessory rentals offer up to two bedrooms with no fee. Large and commercial rentals pay $50.
  • A license runs for two years, with renewal due 30 days in advance.
  • An emergency contact must respond within 24 hours, and utilities must be current.
  • Penalties escalate from a letter to a $250 fine, then $500 plus a six-month suspension, and finally revocation with fines that can reach $1,000 daily.

The city's permits page links each application.

sections.h2: When can a Hamilton seller skip Ohio's disclosure form?
sections.html:
Estates and rentals feed a lot of Hamilton sales, which is why the exceptions in R.C. 5302.30 matter here. A seller acting for someone else, such as an executor, guardian or trustee, does not have to hand over the form. Neither does an heir who inherited the house and did not live in it during the past year. Court-ordered sales, foreclosure sales and deeds in lieu of foreclosure also fall outside the rule.

An investor who bought a rental and never lived in it fits none of those categories. Having tenants in the house changes nothing, so that seller still owes the buyer a completed form. The statute lists each category, and a title agent can say which one fits you.

sections.h2: Butler County Auditor and the deed
sections.html:
The Auditor's Conveyance Department handles every ownership change in Butler County and collects the fees. The conveyance fee works out to $.30 for each $100 of price, or $3 per $1,000, with the price rounded up to the next $100 first. Each parcel adds $0.50.

  • Payment must be cash or a check made out to the Butler County Auditor.
  • Staff cannot make change, and they will not complete a blank check.
  • On a residential rental, the Auditor's endorsement reminds the buyer to file landlord information under R.C. 5323.02.

The deed transfer page has the forms. The title company usually carries the deed in. Have it confirm how to pay before closing day.

sections.h2: When does a quick cash sale suit a Hamilton owner?
sections.html:
Direct sales make sense when repairs would cost more than the house can bear, when tenants are living there, or when an estate has a deadline. Put a written cash offer next to what a repaired listing would net after contractor bills, commissions and months of carrying costs.

Listing with an agent fits a house in decent shape on a street where owner-occupants shop. A cash buyer needs no loan approval and takes the house as it stands, so repairs and showings drop out. Have each buyer write down the price, the closing date and who pays which cost.

At Hamilton's price levels, even modest repair bills eat a noticeable slice of the sale, and that is why owners of dated houses often check direct offers first.

This sequence suits most sales here, whether an investor or a family is buying.

  1. Ask the city or county about the parcel's flood zone and any historic district.
  2. Phone the Building Department about permits from earlier work, and Planning about zoning.
  3. For a former short-term rental, settle the license question.
  4. Work out whether the disclosure form applies. Estate fiduciaries and absentee heirs are often exempt.
  5. Pull together the lease and tenant details when the house is rented, because the buyer files landlord information with the Auditor.
  6. Let the title company draft the deed and bring the exact fee as cash or a check to the Butler County Auditor.

Finally, get the closing date, the split of title and recording costs, and the buyer's plan if a walkthrough turns up a surprise, all in writing.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to run a vacation rental in Hamilton?
faqs.a: Yes, you need a Short-Term Rental License before running or advertising stays under 30 days. Owner-occupied rentals of up to two bedrooms pay no fee, while large or commercial ones pay $50.

faqs.q: How is the Butler County deed fee figured?
faqs.a: The fee is $.30 per $100 of price, which is $3 per $1,000, after rounding up to the next $100. Each parcel adds $0.50. Cash or a check to the Butler County Auditor settles it.

faqs.q: Does an inherited Hamilton house need the state condition form?
faqs.a: Frequently not. Under R.C. 5302.30, an estate fiduciary or an heir who stayed out of the house the previous year is exempt. Ask a title agent about your facts.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Hamilton street?
faqs.a: Hamilton City Schools cover most addresses, though a few fall in Talawanda or Ross Local. The district can look up your address.

faqs.q: Do historic district rules limit what a Hamilton buyer can change?
faqs.a: They can. Exterior work in a district needs Certificate of Appropriateness approval from the Architectural Design Review Board. The districts are Dayton Lane, German Village and Rossville.
